clue.text: Very cold, in general, about one

indicators.note: about means the general's name goes round the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: John Pershing was the American general who led US forces in the First World War
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that, broadly speaking, it is bitterly cold at around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads like 'on the whole', but 'general' is the US commander Pershing; 'about' puts I inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishing is informal British speech for bitterly freezing weather.

clue.text: Literary work of some, range ?

parts.note: read 'range' as a kitchen stove: the thing that heats cooking vessels, hack writing done just to earn a living

explanation.surface: A piece of writing with broad scope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests breadth, but a kitchen range is a stove on which pots boil.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book written quickly for money, keeping the pot on the boil.

clue.text: Dance round the piano in disgust

indicators.note: round means the dance goes about the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
p stands for piano, softly, in music

explanation.surface: Someone dances around the piano in revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to revolt or sicken someone.

clue.text: She secures about fifty ponies

indicators.note: about means the outer words go round the number, holding it inside

parts.note: to secure something with rope is to tie it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A woman tethers around fifty small horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'roughly'; it puts L inside SHE TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelties are Shetland ponies, the small breed from the Shetland Isles.

clue.text: One son needs correcting-fast becoming rude

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: something needing correction is wrong as it stands, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A son must be disciplined, as his fasting has turned to cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs correcting' rearranges SON into NSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means disrespectful or impertinent.

clue.text: Spirited play ?

parts.note: read 'spirited' as full of spirits: a drama named for the dead who haunt the living, by Ibsen

explanation.surface: A lively game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' means lively in the surface; here it means about spectres, Ibsen's 1881 drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's play of 1881 takes its title from phantoms, the dead past haunting the Alving family.

clue.text: Strains familiar to farm workers ?

explanation.surface: Some tunes or melodies are well known to people working the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a wrench or sprain of a joint, and ricks are also the haystacks farmhands build.

clue.text: Beam is put right subsequently

parts.note: after means later, subsequently

explanation.surface: A ray of light is corrected later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put' are link words: R placed before AFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is a sloping timber supporting a roof.

clue.text: State a stipulation

explanation.surface: Declare a requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Condition means a state of being, and also a term that must be met.

clue.text: Looks for certain Indians, say

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: Sikhs are followers of the Sikh religion from the Punjab in India

explanation.surface: Someone searches for particular people from India.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek is to search for.

clue.text: Mechanical parts taken by stage Irishman, retired

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a stage in a process is a step
Pat is the stock nickname for an Irishman

explanation.surface: Engine components are taken off by a theatrical Irishman who has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage Irishman' looks like a theatrical stereotype; split it into STEP and PAT, and 'retired' turns STEPPAT round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tappets are small engine components that open and close the valves.

clue.text: O! my —— is rank" said 21's uncle

definitions.text: O! my —— is rank" said 21's uncle

parts.words: O! my —— is rank" said 21's uncle
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Claudius, the prince's uncle, confesses that his crime of murder stinks to heaven

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's play with a word missing, spoken by the prince's uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is HAMLET; his uncle Claudius says "O, my offence is rank, it smells to heaven" in Act 3.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the crime or misdeed Claudius confesses in his prayer scene.

clue.text: Some P.O.W. letters from a young flier

indicators.note: some means only part of the following letters is taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Part of a prisoner of war's mail comes from a young airman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young flier' suggests a junior pilot, but here it is a baby bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is called an owlet, and it is a bird that flies.

clue.text: A good many scores include eastern draws

parts.note: a lot means a good many

indicators.note: include means the scores take the next letter inside them

parts.note: tries are scores in rugby

explanation.surface: Many football scores include draws from eastern clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scores' suggests twenties or football results; it is rugby TRIES, with E inside making TERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotteries are prize draws decided by chance.

clue.text: Wicked things in these cases, perhaps

definitions.text: Wicked things in these cases, perhaps

parts.words: Wicked things in these cases, perhaps
parts.note: read 'wicked' as 'having a wick': candles are things with wicks, and they sit inside glass cases

explanation.surface: Evil deeds are kept in these containers, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' means evil in the surface, but here it means fitted with a wick, as a candle is.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a case, often glass-sided, that holds a candle or lamp.

clue.text: Feature Athenian bellows-mender as music-maker

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
Francis Flute is the bellows-mender of Athens in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: An Athenian tradesman figures as a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Flute is one of Shakespeare's 'rude mechanicals', who plays Thisbe.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose flute is a wind instrument blown with the nostrils.

clue.text: Prescribed course of conference ?

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescribed programme of treatment at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a regimen of food a doctor may prescribe, and also a formal assembly, as at the Diet of Worms.

clue.text: Will make match by morning — ten, possibly

indicators.note: by means one piece stands next to the other

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A match will be played in the morning, at ten perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TEN into ENT. A Test is a cricket international.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document leaving one's estate.

clue.text: Oarsmen, though without agreement, show vision

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the oarsmen surround the next piece

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A rowing crew, though not in agreement, can see clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: EIGHT goes round YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the ability to see.

clue.text: Means to raise level of oratory ?

definitions.text: Means to raise level of oratory

parts.words: Means to raise level of oratory
parts.note: a raised stage lifts a speaker up, so it is literally a means to raise the speaking above floor level

explanation.surface: A way to improve the standard of public speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise level' suggests improving quality, but it is a physical height.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform is a raised stage from which speeches are made.

clue.text: Sign in the bar remains ?

explanation.surface: A notice in the pub is still there.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a rest is a symbol marking silence within a bar, and the rest means whatever remains.

clue.text: Vehicles carry on in storms

indicators.note: carry means the vehicles hold the next word within them

parts.note: bicycles are vehicles, cycles for short

explanation.surface: Cars and bikes keep going through bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry on' looks like one phrase meaning continue; split it, so CYCLES carry ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclones are violent rotating tropical storms.

clue.text: Where few people live and play ? '

explanation.surface: A place with a small population, and a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village; it is also Shakespeare's tragedy of the Danish prince.

clue.text: Detest alto parts taken by male

indicators.note: parts means the word is broken up and its letters reassembled

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man hates the alto lines he has to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like singing lines; it rearranges ALTO into LOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to hate intensely.

clue.text: Bill's quarries are in the shade; by the plants

indicators.note: by means one piece stands next to the other

parts.note: buff is a pale yellowish-brown shade
aloes are succulent plants

explanation.surface: Someone's prey lies in the shadows beside the shrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is Buffalo Bill Cody, the American frontiersman who hunted bison by the thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bison, the hunter's prey, is commonly known as the buffalo.

clue.text: Get distinguishing mark of animal right off

indicators.note: off means the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a badger is a burrowing animal

explanation.surface: Obtain an animal's identifying marking straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem showing rank or membership.

clue.text: Ornamental wear — associate it with retirement

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing backwards, so the joined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: ARA stands for Associate of the Royal Academy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of decorative clothing is linked with someone's leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associate' is a verb in the surface but the letters ARA (Associate of the Royal Academy); 'with retirement' turns ARAIT round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headpiece worn for decoration.

clue.text: A doctor meets an official from China

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A medic meets a Chinese civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: An amban was a Chinese imperial resident official, as in Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Amban is the title of a Manchu imperial resident commissioner.

clue.text: Little middle garment

explanation.surface: A small item of clothing worn round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the word 'little' is a pair of identical letters, a doublet; a doublet is also a close-fitting man's jacket of old.

clue.text: Most remarkable thing going?

parts.note: read 'going' as departing: the thing one says on leaving, two words with the sense of 'good' and 'by'

explanation.surface: Is this the most amazing thing around?
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' looks like 'in existence' but means leaving; the farewell is built of GOOD and BYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is said by someone leaving.

clue.text: Result of the end opening

indicators.note: the end of the word 'the' is its last letter

parts.note: a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: The outcome of a final match that has just begun.
explanation.definitionFit: An event can mean an outcome, as in 'in the event'.

clue.text: Site meant for café building

indicators.note: building means the letters are put together in a new structure

explanation.surface: A plot of land intended for a coffee shop development.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or café.
